betterCitation: Yehuda Amichai, The Place Where We Are Right, stanza 1, The Selected Poetry of Yehuda Amichai (trans. Bloch and Mitchell, 1986)
reason: The attack that should have killed this one is capitalisation, and it fails. Two lineations circulate. One capitalises every line: From the place where we are right / Flowers will never grow / In the spring, and so on through Is hard and trampled, Like a yard, Dig up the world, Where the ruined, House once stood. The other, the shipped one, capitalises only the sentence openings and leaves flowers and in lower case. Rule 7 makes this decisive, since a verse quotation must carry the poem's own capitals at the line head, and shipping the wrong one would be drift. The two lineations were separated by which witnesses carry a permission credit. The all-capitals version at Journey with Jesus carries NO translator and NO source at all. The lower case version appears in the On Being Project's reproduction under the formal credit to Chana Bloch and Stephen Mitchell and to The Selected Poetry of Yehuda Amichai, University of California Press, copyright 1986, 1996, 2013, and again at A Year of Being Here under the credit The Selected Poetry of Yehuda Amichai, edited and translated from the Hebrew by Chana Bloch and Stephen Mitchell, University of California Press, 1996, where the twelve lines were checked one by one and come out From capital, flowers lower, in lower, The capital, is lower, like lower, But capital, dig lower, like lower, And capital, where lower, house lower. Two credited witnesses agree against two uncredited ones, so the shipped wording and its lower case f stand. The cut is clean: stanza one is three lines and ends on a full stop after in the spring. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, and the file should say so rather than pretend otherwise. The book itself was not opened. The Internet Archive holds only the 1996 University of California Press printing, as a lending copy whose search-inside is closed, and the 1986 Harper and Row first edition was not reachable; the search budget ran out before a scholarly page citation could be found. So no witness was seen that places this particular poem inside the 1986 volume. What supports the 1986 date is the translation copyright line itself, copyright 1986, 1996, 2013 by Chana Bloch and Stephen Mitchell, which is direct evidence that the Bloch and Mitchell English of this book dates from 1986, and the source names 1986 as the year of the published translation whose wording it uses, which is what rule 4 asks. That is enough to ship, but the evidence field overstates when it says the 1986 first edition was confirmed in library listings: confirming that an edition exists is not confirming that this poem is in it, and the note should carry that distinction plainly. A small correctable point, offered above and not a refutation: the book is titled The Selected Poetry of Yehuda Amichai and the source drops the definite article. Restoring it with both translators' full names runs to 141 characters, one over the limit, so the betterCitation keeps the full title and gives the translators by surname at 127 characters; the verifier's line at 137 is shippable as it stands and the choice is the editor's. Everything else clears. Attribution: Amichai's own poem, not on the misattribution list, the poet in his own voice, no speaker to name. Scope: Hebrew original of the late 1950s, English of 1986, poetry, not scripture, not a lyric, nothing needing a warning. Tag: Poetry. Cap: shipped.js gives yehuda amichai at 0 of 3, not banned, nothing shipped, no near opening, one appearance in the month's proposals. Source line leads with the name and carries no dash. Theme: the place where we are right is hard and trampled, which is the corrective a month about what is owed needs, since it turns the reader's certainty back on itself rather than arming it.
